blocks.content: Most debugging starts with knowing which phase a Pod is stuck in. The phase tells you whose problem it is: the scheduler's, the image registry's, or your container's.

items: Pending: not placed on a node yet, usually resources or scheduling rules
Running: placed and at least one container is up
Failed: a container exited non-zero and will not be retried
CrashLoopBackOff: it starts, dies, and Kubernetes is pausing before the next try

blocks.content:
kubectl get pod web -o wide
kubectl describe pod web      # events are at the bottom
kubectl logs web --previous   # logs from the crashed attempt

blocks.title: Read events first
blocks.content: The Events section of `kubectl describe` explains a Pending or CrashLoopBackOff Pod far more often than the container logs do.
